newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells chemical firm stake for $160 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells chemical firm stake for $160 mln.

text.p: Bulgaria has agreed the sale of a 60 percent stake in its Sodi Devnya chemical complex to U.S. firm General Chemical Group Inc for $160 million, deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.
He told state television General Chemical had pledged investments of $118 million over the next five years.
Six foreign companies submitted bids to the Privatisation Agency for the sale, and Gechev said General Chemical's bid was $40 million more than its nearest rival.

The plant exports 10 to 12 percent of the calcinated soda traded in the world. Quarries next to the plant will remain in state hands and the company will have to agree terms with the government for raw material supplies.
General Chemical must pay 10 percent on the day of signing, and the remainder within 30 days, Gechev said.
Sodi-Devnya, which can process 1.2 million tonnes of calcinated soda annually, currently operates at 80 percent of capacity and its net profit for last year was $3.5 million.
Its export markets include the Far East, the Middle East, Latin America and western Europe.
The chemical giant is one of 15 state enterprises which the heavily-indebted government plans to sell by year-end.
Privatisations and closure of loss-making state firms are key conditions set by the International Monetary Fund for Bulgaria to receive any new funding.
